title: Duke's 70th birthday at the White House
summary: They recall the 1970 White House party where Whaley led the orchestra for Joe Williams, sat near Moynihan and Mahalia Jackson, and never received photographs.

blocks.x: Right. But in my basement right here, in Long Island on the wall, there's a picture of you on the wall with this great group in 1970, at Duke's 70th birthday party at the White House. Duke Ellington and President Nixon and you're standing next to Earl Hines.
Hey, what's the other guy from here, had the -- he was running the pictures?
Willis Conover, is that the one?
No, he was from here. He was from New York.
Joe Morgan?
No, he's in the picture business.
I don't know where or who he was. I know that Willis Conover was mainly responsible for M.C.'ing the show.
Yeah, he M.C.'ed it, yeah. But this guy, he was in the back of the pictures. Oh, I never thought I'd forget his name.
Did he ever send you copies of those pictures from the White House?
No.
He didn't?
No, I never got any. When he entered my house, I got the letter from the President inviting me. I think it's on there, I'm not sure. I know I had it there.
Yes, he had the invitations. It was a most remarkable affair. You were there, along with all the dignitaries, not people --
You know the Senator from New York now? Moynihan?
Yeah.
Well, he was there. He was sitting
right -- two seats from me. Yeah, at that table. And what's the singer, the blues singer?
[Marilyn Mayo.]
No, no, the girl that sings -- she don't sing in no theaters. She sings in churches. Joe Bostick's got her.
I can't remember him.
She sang -- what did she sing? She sang a song, down there.
At the White House?
Yeah. Didn't she sing a song down there?
I don't think she did.
No, no, she didn't sing.
I don't think so. [Marilyn Mayo] was the lady that sang -- Joe Williams sang, let my people go.
Yeah, Joe --
And [Marilyn Mayo] sang a couple of songs.
Joe was the one that made me direct the band.
Right. "Prelude to A Kiss" is what [Marilyn Mayo] sang, if I remember.
I'm trying to remember -- oh, she's an old time singer.
Not Mahalia Jackson.
Mahalia Jackson.
Was she there?
Sure, she was there, sitting at the same table with me.
But she didn't sing, I don't think.
No, she didn't sing. Yeah, Mahalia Jackson.
Mahalia Jackson, yes.
Yeah.
